labelling.rule: 3 Heat Extreme Core = highest mean total SHAP; 1 Riparian Buffer = most negative mean SHAP(frac_water)+SHAP(ndwi) among the other three (fallback: highest mean frac_water); 0 Ecological Cool Base = lower mean total SHAP of the last two; 2 Transition = the last one

clusters.name: Ecological Cool Base
clusters.reason: lower mean total SHAP of the last two clusters

clusters.name: Riparian Buffer
clusters.reason: most negative mean SHAP(frac_water) + SHAP(ndwi) among the non-hottest clusters

zones.name: Ecological Cool Base
zones.description: Ecological Cool Base: 14,548 km² in 2025 (26% of the study area), mean observed LST 32.9 °C. Main warming drivers: NDWI (+0.63 °C), Tree cover (+0.02 °C), Cropland (+0.01 °C). Main cooling drivers: NDBI (-2.69 °C), NDVI (-2.15 °C), Night-time lights (-0.07 °C). Largest shares in Muzaffarnagar (23%), Meerut (20%), Bulandshahr (14%).

recommendations.rationale: In the final model, raising NDVI by 0.07 in every cell (zone median 0.38 → 0.45), i.e. greening within the existing land covers is associated with a mean LST change of -0.38 °C over the zone's 14,548 cells (95% CI -0.46 to -0.29 °C). This is a model-based ceteris-paribus estimate, not a causal effect. The target is the feasibility bound (the zone's own 90th/10th percentile, or the maximum step).

In the final model, raising tree cover by 20 percentage points in every cell (zone median 25% → 45%) is associated with a mean LST change of -0.34 °C over the zone's 14,548 cells (95% CI -0.41 to -0.26 °C). The land is taken from the other land covers (including other vegetation) in proportion to their shares, mostly cropland (-14 pp) and impervious cover (-4.5 pp); NDVI, NDWI and NDBI follow through the land-cover coupling. This is a model-based ceteris-paribus estimate, not a causal effect. The target is the feasibility bound (the zone's own 90th/10th percentile, or the maximum step).

In the final model, lowering cropland by 20 percentage points in every cell (zone median 49% → 29%) is associated with a mean LST change of -0.28 °C over the zone's 14,548 cells (95% CI -0.32 to -0.23 °C). The land is given to the other land covers (including other vegetation) in proportion to their shares, mostly tree cover (+10 pp) and impervious cover (+6.4 pp); NDVI, NDWI and NDBI follow through the land-cover coupling. This is a model-based ceteris-paribus estimate, not a causal effect. The target is the feasibility bound (the zone's own 90th/10th percentile, or the maximum step).

In the final model, raising edge density by 48 in every cell (zone median 68.5 → 117) is associated with a mean LST change of -0.07 °C over the zone's 14,548 cells (95% CI -0.11 to -0.03 °C). This is a model-based ceteris-paribus estimate, not a causal effect. The target is the feasibility bound (the zone's own 90th/10th percentile, or the maximum step).
